When writing a (long) manuscript, it is often useful to add a glossary.
With [LaTeX] the glossary is properly managed with the [acronym package](https://ctan.org/pkg/acronym).
But, neither [Pandoc] nor [bookdown] provide a proper way to do this (see [this issue](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/issues/199)).
\
With [bookdown], the common basic proposed solution is to put the acronyms in a data file (e.g. in csv format or xslx) and then render a the glossary page
(see e.g. [@yongfu; @ewfrees]).
However, these simple solutions do not link from the acronym in the text body to the glossary page, as is the case with the  [LaTeX] [acronym package](https://ctan.org/pkg/acronym).

My solution effectively use the above  basic solution with the adds of an anchor on each acronyms and terms:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="true" code-summary="Show the code"}
# library(tidyverse)
# library(magrittr)
load_descr <- function(descr,data_file, data_dir="data") {
  data_path = xfun::native_encode(file.path(data_dir, data_file))
  descr$data <- readr::read_csv(data_path, col_types = readr::cols(), trim_ws = TRUE, skip_empty_rows = TRUE)
  invisible(descr)
}

#' print_acro
#'
#' @param data_file a csv file with two column: abbrv, descr
#' @param data_dir directory where the data file is stored
#' @param id_prefix prefix for the identifier
#' @param class the class for the `abbrv`
#' @param indent a string use for indentation
#' @param glue_template the template use to print the acronym
#'
#' @return The acronym in a format 
#'
print_acro <- function(data_file, data_dir = "data", id_prefix = "acro", class = "acronym-item",
                      indent='', glue_template = "default") {
  descr <- list() %>%  load_descr(data_file, data_dir)
  # generate an id in the format id_prefix-abbrv
  descr$data %<>%
    dplyr::mutate(id=paste0(id_prefix, "-",stringr::str_replace_all(abbrv," ", "-")))

  if (glue_template == "default") {
    glue_template <- "\n
<<indent>>[<<abbrv>>]{#<<id>> .<<class>>}
\n"
  }

  acro <- descr$data
  print(glue::glue_data(acro,glue_template,indent='',.open = "<<",.close = ">>"))
}
```
:::


## Example
For instance, if you have the following csv data file in `acro.csv`:

+-------+-----------------+
| abbrv | descr           |
+-------+-----------------+
| 2D    | two-dimension   |
+-------+-----------------+
| 3D    | three-dimension |
+-------+-----------------+

the following markdown will be generated using `print_acro(acro.csv)`
```markdown
[2D]{#acro-2D .acronym-item}
:   two-dimension

[3D]{#acro-3D .acronym-item}
:   three-dimension
```
One can link to the glossary page as follows:

```markdown
In [2D](#acro-2D){.acroterm} you get [...]
```

[Bookdown] is then able to generate a link the anchor in the glossary page (i.e. where you have called  `print_acro(acro.csv)`).
\
Next, if you're using [Rstudio] (or any IDE that does the same), you can add a _snippet_, such as:
```markdown
snippet acro
	[${1:acro}](#acro-${1:acro}){.acroterm}
```
With this, one can easily add an acronym in the text body, and that, for any [pandoc] output format!

:::{.callout-tip}
You can change the snippet to include the `abbr` HTML tag, but this work only with HTML like output  :frowning_face:
:::

Nevertheless, it remains that the management of plural forms is not yet possible (although  [LaTeX] [acronym package](https://ctan.org/pkg/acronym) allows it)...
In my opinion, the only way that may allow such functionality is to define some specific (`R`) function (or a specific package?).

> **Edit**: I found recently this package <https://github.com/yonicd/glossaries> (but not curently tested)
